prompt: Interstates have no traffic lights, stop signs or cross traffic. What does safe interstate driving still demand from you?
choices: Less attention than city streets, since nothing crosses your path
Constant alertness, since high speeds leave less time to react
Keeping up with the fastest cars, even above the speed limit
Setting cruise control so you can relax on long stretches
explanation: Controlled access makes interstates efficient, but at high speed situations change fast and you travel farther before you can react. Stay fully alert, scan far ahead and check your mirrors often.
ref: State driver handbooks (e.g. TN p.82, IL p.89)

prompt: You come upon a crash that you did not see happen. Police and an ambulance are already there, and you are not involved. What should you do?
choices: Pull over nearby in case the crews need extra help
Slow to a crawl so you can see what happened
Stop and wait to give the police a statement
Keep driving carefully past without stopping
explanation: Stop at a crash only if you are involved or emergency help has not arrived yet. Otherwise keep moving carefully, without staring, so you don't get in the way of responders or cause another crash.
ref: State driver handbooks (e.g. TN p.104, PA p.85, NY p.77)
